transcript: Want to save PowerPoint as video? You have two sensible options, and they suit different jobs. Here's how to pick the right one for your deck.
PowerPoint's own export plays your animations exactly as designed, with your real voice. The catch? Stumble on slide 12, and you re-record slide 12.
A dedicated converter reads your speaker notes aloud, adds captions and times everything to the speech. The trade-off is a synthetic voice instead of your own.
Take one headline about new starters' laptops. Record it yourself, and every change means a new take. Type it into the notes, and a change is one quick edit.
Many people use both. A leader's quarterly message suits their own voice, while an onboarding module that changes every few months suits a converter.
Ordinary slides in, extraordinary video out. On Pro, a.i. directs your video, tightening the story and timing each scene. Try Basic first at powerpoint2vid.com.
